The annual law that provides the Defense Department's money. The [NDAA](ndaa-annual.qmd) sets policy and authorizes amounts; this act makes funds available to obligate, account by account, and attaches general provisions that limit how they may be used. The series began with the National Military Establishment Appropriation Act, 1950 (Pub. L. 81-434), the first single appropriation for the newly unified military.

::: {.official-links}

:::

## Key provisions

- Titles I-VII: military personnel; operation and maintenance; procurement; research, development, test and evaluation; revolving funds; other programs; related agencies.
- Title VIII general provisions recur each year, on transfers, reprogramming, multiyear contracts, and limits on the use of funds.
- Sec. 8005 (FY2026): general transfer authority of up to $6 billion between accounts, only for higher-priority, unforeseen military requirements and never for an item Congress has denied.
- Military construction and family housing are funded in a separate act, the Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies appropriations.

## Why it matters

Authorization without appropriation spends nothing, so this act is where Congress's control of the military is most concrete. Funding prohibitions in it have ended or limited operations, as the [Case-Church Amendment](case-church-1973.qmd) and the [Boland Amendments](boland-1982.qmd) did, and its transfer authority ([Sec. 8005 transfers](sec8005-transfer.qmd)) sets how far the Department can move money Congress assigned elsewhere. When the act is late, the Department runs on continuing resolutions that generally bar new programs and production increases. Members and staff who want to change defense policy without a new authorization usually look here first.

## Current status

The most recent full-year act is for fiscal year 2026, enacted as Division A of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Pub. L. 119-75, signed February 3, 2026). Fiscal year 2027 began under a continuing resolution (Pub. L. 119-103) that runs through December 11, 2026. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [Constitution (war powers)](constitution-war-powers.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [Sec. 8005 transfers](sec8005-transfer.qmd), [Presidential drawdown (Sec. 506)](pda-506.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 10 U.S.C.](title10-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Building the national security state ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 4: The power of the purse](../study/units/purse.qmd) (core reading).
- **Who's involved.** [House Appropriations](../whos-who.qmd#hac), [Senate Appropriations](../whos-who.qmd#sac), [DoD](../whos-who.qmd#dod).
- **Member lenses.** [Rep. Jason Crow](../members/crow.qmd): No Funds for Iran War Act.
